name: intervals-and-topk
prompt:
Write a module `solution.py` with two functions:
1. merge_intervals(intervals: list[list[int]]) -> list[list[int]] — merge all overlapping/adjacent closed intervals, sorted, tolerating an empty list.
2. top_k(nums: list[int], k: int) -> list[int] — the k most frequent values, ties broken by larger value first, no duplicates in the result.
Answer with the full file content in one ```python block and nothing else.
test:
from solution import merge_intervals, top_k
assert merge_intervals([[1,3],[2,6],[8,10],[15,18]]) == [[1,6],[8,10],[15,18]]
assert merge_intervals([[1,4],[4,5]]) == [[1,5]]
assert merge_intervals([]) == []
assert top_k([3,1,3,2,3,2], 2) == [3,2]
assert top_k([1,2,3,4], 1) == [4]
assert top_k([5,5,5], 3) == [5]
print("OK")
